items.label: Real-time subtitle clarity
items.summary: Keep subtitles clear, fast, and stable enough that the wearer can trust them in live conversation.

items.label: Trustworthy memory support
items.summary: Remember names, faces, and prior context without pretending certainty or creating corrupted recall.

items.label: Low-friction assistance
items.summary: Deliver one-line help and visible support without creating command overhead or social awkwardness.

items.label: Privacy vs usefulness
items.summary: Helpful assistive behavior should not quietly slide into invasive capture or retention.

items.label: Latency vs richness
items.summary: The system should provide timely help without overloading the runtime with richer but slower processing.

items.label: Discreet UX vs visual clarity
items.summary: Display behavior should remain socially acceptable while still being readable in motion and noise.

items.label: Frame-touch-only V1
items.summary: V1 explicit interaction should happen through frame touches, not voice commands.

items.label: Phone-first runtime
items.summary: Heavy processing should primarily happen on the phone, with cloud optional where clearly justified.

items.label: Core-deepening over sprawl
items.summary: Prefer work that improves subtitle quality, memory trust, and visual UX over broad feature expansion.

items.label: Core Deepening
items.summary: Bias toward subtitle, memory, confidence, and architecture improvements that increase daily-use value.

items.label: Constraint Pressure
items.summary: Surface battery, latency, privacy, and usability limits early so weak directions are killed quickly.

items.label: Implementation Grounding
items.summary: Reason from actual repo files, app docs, and build truth instead of generic ideation.
